summary.overview:
- Daniel Smith appointed as new MD for buy/sell mandates under £100k; Andrew focuses on larger acquisitions and roll-ups.
- Project McLaren delayed with Ziff Davis unresponsive for 13 days; new lead John from MPG Marketing has extensive acquisition experience (14 deals).
- Skyview offer pending response from Anton; valuation target set at £40–50m, aiming for 7x EBITDA; Clint Kendall re-engaged as potential partner.
- Project Castle (99 Ads) launched; named by Daniel after team discussion, moving forward under Ahmed's leadership.
- CTV Media engagement delayed despite client payment; expected to resume activities by July/August.
- Nova project gaining interest from Australian and American buyers; concerns about business continuity and retainer strength raised.
- Two buyers withdrew from Extermina; new interest from Seattle web design company requires follow-up by Ahmed.
- Leslie Francis project has two buyers; one offer pending, buyer's advisor to be consulted.
- Deal engine shows strong performance from front runners Peter Stubbings, Peter Hogan, and Robert Felters; Charlie Norton's campaign slow due to geographical restrictions.
- High-value client Gary Smith to implement instant messaging sequence for better communication, coordination underway with Danny Farnam.
summary.short_summary: Daniel Smith has been appointed as the new Managing Director for buy/sell mandates under £100k, while Andrew will concentrate on larger acquisitions and roll-ups. Project McLaren has faced delays due to unresponsiveness from Ziff Davis, but a new lead, John from MPG Marketing, has been introduced, bringing significant acquisition experience with 14 deals. Skyview's offer is pending a response from Anton, with a valuation target set between £40-50m aiming for 7x EBITDA; Clint Kendall has been re-engaged as a potential partner. Project Castle, named 99 Ads, was launched under Ahmed's leadership. Engagement with CTV Media is delayed despite client payment, with activities expected to resume by July/August. The Nova project is attracting interest from Australian and American buyers, raising concerns about business continuity. Two buyers withdrew from Extermina, while new interest from a Seattle web design company needs follow-up by Ahmed. Leslie Francis has two buyers, with one offer pending and the buyer's advisor to be consulted. The deal engine shows strong performance from Peter Stubbings, Peter Hogan, and Robert Felters, although Charlie Norton's campaign is slow due to geographical restrictions. High-value client Gary Smith is set to implement an instant messaging sequence for improved communication, with coordination ongoing with Danny Farnam.
